I caught this via `git reflog` (which showed 4 "cherry-pick:" entries) before verifying, treated it as a lease violation (diff far outside packages/client/src/router.tsx, plus injecting other tasks' unrelated commits into this branch's history), and reverted it: `git reset --hard` back to the original base tip (9ee5a1b) and reapplied only the router.tsx patch and the new test file via `git apply`, which is the state verified above. No commit was made — the working tree containing that clean, in-footprint diff was verified once more (git diff --stat showing only router.tsx + the new test file) and the worktree was then removed since this run ends blocked. This is a plan/graph-ordering gap, not something a same-footprint retry against this base branch can resolve: either this task's base branch needs to be re-pointed past loop/nav-shell--route-fixups (and ideally the e2e-migration siblings) before re-running, or its footprint needs to be widened to cover the 2 pre-existing landing-assertion test files (and, for the e2e gate, the migrated specs) — a decision for the orchestrating layer, not this drive.
